scope: local HTTP/domain/durability; no browser rendering, cartridge bridge or public deployment acceptance

results.name: Loopback service advertises only the implemented ordinary-item profile
HTTP demo is served with restrictive browser-origin and script policies
Cross-origin browser calls and hostile Host headers are refused
Malformed transport payloads and oversized JSON cannot mutate the World
Session tokens are generated, hashed at rest, and authorize only their own player
Join validation rejects injected player identity and invalid names
Two simultaneous clients produce exactly one accepted pickup
Identical request retries return the original durable receipt with no new mutation
Request IDs cannot be reused for changed payloads or changed revisions
Stale rejected receipts remain rejected after later World changes
Intents reject unknown versions, extra fields, invented outcomes and owner spoofing
Movement is one cardinal tile and rejects boundaries and diagonal/teleport requests
Pickup and transfer enforce authoritative range and ownership
Earn, equip, trade, store and retrieve preserve one stable item instance
Gathering issues one server-defined claim and cannot be farmed by retry or new request IDs
Consumption heals only the authoritative player and tombstones the item
Vendor and recipe use the same issuance rules and atomically consume inputs
Drop then pickup retains issuer, claim, quantity and item identity
Projection enforces 12 actor slots and exactly 64 persistent bytes without losing server records
Profile capacities refuse issuance instead of evicting identity or receipts
Unknown issuers are rejected even when a voucher is correctly signed
Explicit issuer/version mapping accepts a signed destination-bound voucher once
Voucher tampering, wrong destination and unmapped versions are rejected
Colon-containing issuer, source and claim IDs preserve separate signed identities
Second local process cannot concurrently open the same data directory
Restart preserves sessions, inventory, World revision and retry receipts
Checksum corruption fails closed and never replaces the previous World
A failed snapshot write is not acknowledged and blocks further actions until restart
A directory fsync failure after rename recovers exactly one receipt on retry after restart
Receipt capacity never evicts an earlier replay-protection record
Offline backup validates and restores to a new directory with the same accepted outcome
Accepted HTTP outcomes survive a killed process and automatic dead-PID lock recovery

relationship: Included standalone host-service draft. This suite exercises HTTP/domain/storage; it does not execute the HTML or a cartridge bridge.
